headline.title: First flakes for Northern Vermont.
headline.text: Up to {{s:1}} on the summit of Jay Peak Friday morning to early Saturday. 18 of the 19 resorts close to opening get nights cold enough to make snow, mostly in White Mountains and Northern Vermont. Killington typically opens first, around Nov 8.

snowshoe.headline: Freeze Watch issued October 16 at 4:25PM EDT until October 18 at 9:00AM EDT by NWS Charleston WV
snowshoe.text: * WHAT...Sub-freezing temperatures as low as 28 possible. * WHERE...Portions of southeast Ohio, southwest Virginia, and central, northeast, northern, southeast, and southern West Virginia. * WHEN...From late Saturday night through Sunday morning. * IMPACTS...Frost and freeze conditions could kill crops, other sensitive vegetation and possibly damage unprotected outdoor plumbing.

camelback.text: * WHAT...Sub-freezing temperatures in the upper 20s to low 30s possible. * WHERE...In New Jersey, Sussex County. In Pennsylvania, Carbon and Monroe Counties. * WHEN...From late Saturday night through Sunday morning. * IMPACTS...Frost and freeze conditions could kill crops, other sensitive vegetation and possibly damage unprotected outdoor plumbing.

sevensprings.text: * WHAT...Sub-freezing temperatures as low as 25 possible. * WHERE...A portion of central Pennsylvania. * WHEN...From late Saturday night through Sunday morning. * IMPACTS...Frost and freeze conditions could kill crops, other sensitive vegetation and possibly damage unprotected outdoor plumbing.

BTV.excerpt:
Gusty winds to continue through Saturday with much cooler temperatures on the way. First round of snowfall expected for the high peaks tonight.
Next week continues to trend very quiet as high pressure builds in across the area with temperatures near normal and high confidence in an extended dry period of weather.

GYX.excerpt:
An approaching cold front continues rain chances into this evening with a couple of gusty thunderstorms possible in southern NH.
A seasonably cold airmass and gusty winds arrive behind the cold front to start the weekend, with wintry conditions across the higher terrain.
Mild and dry conditions look to persist from Sunday through much of next week as high pressure dominates over the Northeast.

PHI.excerpt:
A strong cold front will cross the region late this afternoon and this evening with severe weather possible.
Frost and freeze conditions are expected for Saturday night into Sunday morning with another round of frost possible for Sunday night into Monday morning.
Uncertainty persists regarding a nor'easter developing off the coast of the southern Mid-Atlantic that may cause unsettled conditions and hazardous marine impacts early next week.

writeups.name: Vermont
writeups.title: Just a coating for the high peaks.
paras: Light snow Friday morning to early Saturday: Jay Peak {{s:1}}, Stowe {{s:0.7}} at the summits, though the models range from {{r:0.1,4.8}} at Jay Peak. Rain mixes in even up high at times.
Next two days: summit temperatures from {{t:21}} to {{t:56}}, with up to {{s:1.5}} of snow and gusts near {{w:44}} up top.
Killington usually opens first here, around Nov 8. Jay Peak gets the most hours cold enough to make snow this week (about 26).
NWS Burlington forecasters, Friday 2:24 PM: "Gusty winds to continue through Saturday with much cooler temperatures on the way. First round of snowfall expected for the high peaks tonight."
writeups.outlook: Days 8 to 14: NOAA's outlook leans warmer than normal and slightly drier than normal.

insights.text: First flakes: about {{s:1}} at the summit Friday morning to early Saturday (models {{r:0.1,4.8}}). It starts as rain ({{l:0.89}}), even at the summit, then changes to snow Friday night as colder air arrives. It won't last: highs reach {{t:49}} Monday.
Cold enough to make snow Saturday morning to Sunday morning: about 26 hours at or below {{t:26}} at mid-mountain, counting humidity. Whether the guns run is up to the resort.
Typically opens around Nov 27, 42 days out.
